properties.name: A spawned shared daemon inherits nothing it should not: a session of its own, none of its launcher's descriptors, and its exit status collected by the client that started it
properties.rationale:
THE CAUSE, confirmed on main 293f957 before the fix (fact:a-spawned-shared-daemon-keeps-every-file-descriptor-its-parent-left-open-2026-10-03): spawn_daemon set the daemon's stdin, stdout and stderr and its process group, and nothing else. std::process::Command closes no descriptor; it relies on close-on-exec, which holds for descriptors Rust opens and not for those the client INHERITED from its launcher (flock(1)'s lock, a shell's redirection, an editor's pipe). So a daemon meant to outlive its session kept each one for its whole life (--idle-timeout, 120 minutes by default), and stayed in its launcher's session and terminal. Measured with the new test on main: the launcher's file on fd 7 in the daemon, flock(1)'s lock on fd 3 still held after the client and flock had exited, the daemon's session id equal to the launcher's.

THE CLASS is what a daemon keeps of the process that started it, and what it leaves behind for it. The same function dropped the daemon's Child without waiting, so a daemon that exited while its client ran (a lost lock race, an idle expiry, --stop-shared, a re-election) stayed a zombie of that client: measured on main with the new test (state Z under the live client), which is the cause of fact:a-long-lived-shared-proxy-leaks-zombie-children-42-in-seven-days, whose spawn site had not been established. Every other process reflow2 starts (git, kill, ps, the wall check's python) is waited for and ends before its parent. The one other long-lived process in the repo, the Stop hook's graph probe (tools/loop_nudge.py), is Python: subprocess.Popen's default close_fds=True and its start_new_session=True already give it both guarantees, so it was left unchanged.

MARKED CLOSE-ON-EXEC, NOT CLOSED: std reports a failed exec to the parent through a close-on-exec pipe of its own, and closing every descriptor in pre_exec would close that pipe and turn a failed exec into a reported success.

NOT DONE: Windows. reflow2 ships no Windows build and shared mode cannot stop or replace a server there; the equivalents (PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST, which stable std does not expose, and DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP) are written down at shared::detach. A daemon's environment and working directory are still inherited on purpose: the rendezvous reads a relative store path against the daemon's working directory. NOT MEASURED HERE: the macOS walk on a Mac (a unit test runs the walk on Linux).
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: shared::detach is the one place a process reflow2 starts to outlive its parent is detached. In the child, before exec: setsid (its own session and process group, no controlling terminal; replaces process_group(0)), then every descriptor above stderr marked close-on-exec (close_range with CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC on Linux 5.11+, otherwise a walk to the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE, bounded at 2^20). spawn_daemon collects the daemon's exit status on a thread. libc is a named direct dependency (already in the tree). The --shared help text and docs/collaborating.md say what the server no longer keeps.
